raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ### Benchmark: Qwen3-32B + EAGLE3, AV on `main` vs. with the verify-cost fix **Setup** - **Hardware:** GB200, one GPU per server (TP1). All three servers ran at the same time on separate GPUs of one node, so the arms share wall-clock conditions. - **Target:** `Qwen/Qwen3-32B` (bf16). **Drafter:** `RedHatAI/Qwen3-32B-speculator.eagle3`. - **vLLM:** Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). - Baseline: `main` @ `642c18d64c`. - Fix: `fix-av-cost-model` @ `83d31d56eb` plus working-tree changes. - **Server flags (all arms):** ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-32B -tp 1 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-model-len 8192 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size": 2048}' \ --speculative-config '' ``` - **Arms:** | Arm | Code | `--speculative-config` | |---|---|---| | fixed K=3 | `main` | `{"method": "eagle3", "model": "", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "enable_adaptive_verification": false}` | | AV, K=7 | `main` | `{"method": "eagle3", "model": "", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "enable_adaptive_verification": true}` | | AV, K=7 + fix | fix branch | same as above | - **Workload:** SPEED-Bench `throughput_2k`, all categories, chat endpoint. Qwen3's default chat template, so thinking mode is on. ```bash vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen3-32B --dataset-name speed_bench \ --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_2k --speed-bench-output-len 2048 \ --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \ --request-rate inf --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $N \ --num-warmups $(( C < 16 ? C : 16 )) \ --temperature 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --seed 0 ``` - Concurrency and prompt count (C / N): 1 / 24, 8 / 64, 32 / 128, 64 / 256, 128 / 384, 256 / 768. - Each server first ran a discarded warm pass (C=64, 128 prompts, seed 1). - One run per arm. Run-to-run noise on this setup is about 2–4%: fixed K=3 spread that much across three separate runs. **Fitted cost terms (from the fix arm's startup profile)** - Context reads: **0.274 ms per request**, **0.0001 ms per token**. Relative RMS error of the linear fit: 0.8%. - 113 of the profiled sizes run several tokens per request (R = 256, T = 272–2,048). Their context cost stays flat at about 70 ms, so on dense attention a draft adds no context-read cost. **Results: output throughput (tok/s)** | Concurrency | fixed K=3 | AV, K=7 (`main`) | AV, K=7 + fix | fix vs. `main` | fix vs. fixed K=3 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 132.3 | 122.3 | 127.4 | +4.2% | −3.7% | | 8 | 910.4 | 750.3 | 863.6 | **+15.1%** | −5.1% | | 32 | 2,477.3 | 2,001.9 | 2,396.9 | **+19.7%** | −3.2% | | 64 | 3,597.2 | 3,170.5 | 3,356.2 | +5.9% | −6.7% | | 128 | 4,174.1 | 3,756.7 | 4,179.1 | **+11.2%** | +0.1% | | 256 | 3,836.7 | 3,811.8 | 3,916.5 | +2.7% | +2.1% | **Acceptance length:** | Concurrency | 1 | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 256 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | fixed K=3 | 1.96 | 1.92 | 1.95 | 1.96 | 1.97 | 1.97 | | AV `main` | 1.97 | 1.78 | 1.61 | 1.58 | 1.92 | 1.94 | | AV + fix | 2.07 | 2.02 | 2.04 | 2.03 | 1.97 | 1.98 |

nodes.body: Closing because https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62960 seems like the better long-term approach

Thanks @TheEpicDolphin for having a look at my PR! I made my PR a draft because the approach works for full attention, but it might not work for SWA or GDN models. So far, I’ve only tested it with Qwen3-4B, and I’m not sure whether it generalizes to all model architectures.

Not sure if we would be fine to merge this [PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62960) as a first step toward a more general solution. Alternatively, someone could open a new PR with a more comprehensive approach!

+def _profile_context_split(monkeypatch, max_num_reqs, per_req, per_token_context):
+    """Profiles a manager whose verify cost is 10 + 0.01 / token, plus per_req
+    per request and per_token_context per token for context reads."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        adaptive_module,
+        "get_tp_group",
+        lambda: SimpleNamespace(broadcast_object=lambda obj, src: obj),
+    )
+    manager = AdaptiveVerificationManager.__new__(AdaptiveVerificationManager)
+    manager.req_states = SimpleNamespace(
+        max_num_batched_tokens=64, max_num_reqs=max_num_reqs
+    )
+    manager.num_speculative_steps = 7
+    manager.num_bonus_tokens = 1
+    manager._cudagraph_limit = 64
+
+    sizes = [8, 16, 32, 64]
+    batches = list(manager.batches_to_profile(sizes))
+    assert {b["num_tokens"] for b in batches if b["context_len"] == 0} == set(sizes)
+
+    def sample(num_tokens: int, context_len: int) -> StepTimingSample:
+        num_reqs = min(num_tokens, max_num_reqs)
+        context = per_req * num_reqs + per_token_context * num_tokens
+        return StepTimingSample(
+            forward_ms=10.0 + 0.01 * num_tokens + context * (context_len > 0),
+            drafter_ms=1.0,
+            num_target_tokens=num_tokens,
+            num_reqs=num_reqs,
+            full_cudagraph=True,
+            context_len=context_len,
+        )
+
+    manager.set_initial_cost_curves(
+        [sample(b["num_tokens"], b["context_len"]) for b in batches]
+    )
+    return manager
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("per_req", "per_token_context"),
+    [(0.3, 0.0), (0.1, 0.2)],
+    ids=["dense", "sparse"],
+)
+def test_drafts_are_not_priced_as_new_requests(monkeypatch, per_req, per_token_context):
+    """Profiles up to max_num_reqs run one token per request, so each request's
+    context reads land in the per-token curve unless split out. A draft joins a
+    request already in the batch: it pays only context reads that scale with
+    tokens, which sparse attention has and dense attention doesn't."""
+    manager = _profile_context_split(monkeypatch, 16, per_req, per_token_context)
+
+    assert manager._verify_cost_per_req == pytest.approx(per_req)
+    assert manager.cost_tables is not None
+    verify = manager.cost_tables[1]
+    # 16 requests verifying 1 vs 3 drafts each: the same contexts.
+    np.testing.assert_allclose(verify[64] - verify[32], (0.01 + per_token_context) * 32)
+
+
+def test_context_split_falls_back_to_per_token_pricing(monkeypatch):
+    # Every profile runs one token per request: requests and tokens can't be
+    # told apart, so context stays priced per token, as before.
+    manager = _profile_context_split(monkeypatch, 64, 0.3, 0.0)
+    assert manager._verify_cost_per_req == 0.0
+
+    # Profiling without any context still prices every token, as before.
+    sizes = [8, 16, 32, 64]
+    manager.set_initial_cost_curves(
+        [StepTimingSample(1.0 + t, 1.0, t, t, True, context_len=0) for t in sizes]
+    )
+    assert manager._verify_cost_per_req == 0.0
+    np.testing.assert_allclose(manager.cost_tables[1][sizes], [1.0 + t for t in sizes])
+
+

+        # The captured sizes again without context. Dummy runs pad every request
+        # a graph holds, so the request count can't be varied at a fixed token
+        # count; dropping the context instead isolates what each request's
+        # context reads cost.
+        for num_tokens in capture_sizes:
+            for _ in range(_PROFILE_REPLAYS):
+                yield {"num_tokens": num_tokens, "context_len": 0}
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _estimate_context_cost_per_req(
+        samples: list[StepTimingSample],
+        contextless_samples: list[StepTimingSample],
+    ) -> float:
+        """Verify ms of context reads per request in the batch, independent of
+        how many of its tokens are verified.
+
+        Up to max_num_reqs, profiles run one token per request, so pricing drafts
+        along that curve charges each draft a whole request's context, while a
+        draft joins a request already in the batch. The context's extra cost is
+        a * num_reqs + b * num_tokens: dense attention reads a request's context
+        once (b ~ 0), while sparse attention also indexes and gathers it per
+        token. Larger profiles run several tokens per request, which separates
+        a from b; the verify table keeps b. Returns 0, pricing context per token
+        as before, when the profiles can't separate them."""
+
+        def by_tokens(group: list[StepTimingSample]) -> dict[int, tuple[float, float]]:
+            grouped: defaultdict[int, list[StepTimingSample]] = defaultdict(list)
+            for s in group:
+                if s.full_cudagraph:
+                    grouped[s.num_target_tokens].append(s)
+            return {
+                t: (
+                    float(np.median([s.forward_ms for s in g])),
+                    float(np.median([s.num_reqs for s in g])),
+                )
+                for t, g in grouped.items()
+            }
+
+        with_context = by_tokens(samples)
+        without_context = by_tokens(contextless_samples)
+        sizes = [
+            (with_context[t][1], t, with_context[t][0] - without_context[t][0])
+            for t in sorted(with_context.keys() & without_context.keys())
+            if with_context[t][1] == without_context[t][1] > 0
+        ]
+        if not sizes:
+            return 0.0
+        num_reqs, num_tokens, context_cost = (np.asarray(x) for x in zip(*sizes))
+        if np.all(num_tokens == num_reqs):
+            # One token per request. a and b are indistinguishable, so price
+            # context per-token.
+            return 0.0
+
+        # Solve the following system of equations:
+        #   context_cost = a * num_reqs + b * num_tokens
+        # to find how much of the context cost is per-request vs per-token.
+        design = np.stack([num_reqs, num_tokens], axis=1).astype(np.float64)
+        (a, b), *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(design, context_cost, rcond=None)
+        if b < 0:
+            # Context cost does not scale with number of tokens, so refit it all
+            # per-request.
+            a = np.dot(num_reqs, context_cost) / np.dot(num_reqs, num_reqs)
+        if a <= 0:
+            # Context cost does not scale with the number of requests, so price
+            # context per-token.
+            return 0.0
+        return float(a)
